newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Senator's aide denies links with Sinn Fein.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senator's aide denies links with Sinn Fein.

text.p: An aide to President Bill Clinton's special Ireland envoy on Monday denied reports that she was romantically linked to a convicted Irish Republican Army bomber.

Martha Pope, Chief of Staff to ex-Senator George Mitchell, told reporters on arrival for the latest round of Northern Ireland peace talks Mitchell is chairing that the reports she was linked with Gerry kelly were without foundation.
"I am happy to state categorically that there is no truth in them whatsoever. Indeed I've never met Mr Kelly," Pope said.
Mitchell, tipped to take a senior place in Clinton's next cabinet, also denied the reports, which first surfaced in the British Mail on Sunday newspaper.
Mitchell told reporters as he arrived for the talks that the reports linking Pope with Kelly, a member of the IRA's political wing, Sinn Fein, were false.
"The allegations are scurrilous. They are absolutely and totally false. They are a complete fabrication. The situation is regrettable," said Mitchell.

The reports cast a cloud over the five-month-old Northern Ireland peace talks, in which Mitchell is trying to get pro-British Unionists and pro-Irish nationalists to agree a lasting settlement to end the 27-year-old conflict which has killed 3,200 people.
The negotiations were delayed for months by Unionist attempts to limit the powers of Mitchell because of what they said were his symathies with Irish nationalists.
Mitchell, the U.S. President's Ireland economic adviser, has strongly denied that his mixed Irish ancestry will compromise his neutrality at the talks.

Leading Ulster Unionist Party negotiator Ken Magginnis said as he arrived for the talks: "As far as I am aware these rumours have been around for almost a month now and we know the security services were alerted to it. We have left the matter to them.
"It would be a disaster that something with no substance could affect the talks."
Brid Rogers of the moderate Irish nationalist Social, Democratic and Labour Party said the reports were "clearly a case of dirty tricks at work".
The Mail on Sunday said in a weekend report that British intelligence had investigated reports that Pope, 51, had had weekend trysts with Kelly in Ireland and secret meetings in Northern Ireland.
Both Pope, the first woman Secretary to the U.S. Senate and Kelly denied the report in separate weekend statements.
Pope played a leading role in organising a conference Clinton convened in Washington in May, 1995, to draw investment to Ireland to underpin the fledgling peace process.
Kelly was jailed for life for 1973 bombings carried out by the IRA, which is fighting to end British rule of the province and reunite it with Ireland.
He escaped from Northern Ireland's top-security Maze Prison in 1983 along with 37 other IRA convicts and spent four years at large before being recaptured in Amsterdam.
He was returned to prison after lengthy extradition hearings and was released in 1989. He is now one of the negotiating team Sinn Fein would like to send to the peace talks.
Sinn Fein is barred from the talks until the IRA restores a ceasefire it broke in February with bombs in Britain, Germany and Northern Ireland.
